Chapter 19 of 19

The 3:17 Freight

False Creek Flats / East Van rail corridor
The story

At 3:17 in the morning, a freight train crosses the East Van rail corridor by the False Creek flats. It is always 3:17. If you happen to be awake and look at a clock, it will say 3:17, and so will the next clock, and the one after that.

The Freight is how Terminal City throws things away. Failed repairs, old versions of a corner, objects that ended up in the wrong place, the residue of a long night: anything the city cannot reconcile in the current build gets loaded onto the Freight and carried out. Nobody has explained who does the loading, and the city is not in a hurry to find out. The train seems to go on longer than it should. Cars repeat. It does not matter how many.

The Old Line keeps what must be remembered. The Freight removes what cannot remain. When it has gone, the fog comes in behind it and the rebuild begins. Three seventeen. Hold time. Load it out. Do not count the cars.

Terminal City is an original fictional mythology inspired by Vancouver’s geography, weather, wildlife, infrastructure, art, and electronic music. It makes no claim to historical, Indigenous, or religious tradition. Real places are used as settings; the operating system layered on them is invented. Photograph reality. Alter the evidence. Never illustrate the whole myth.
